concerns.location: research.md:Algorithmic Design — TV calculation row; plan.md Phase 4
concerns.text: The conditional TV reference distribution is unspecified/ambiguous. research.md gives a single formula `tv = 0.5 * np.sum(np.abs(freq - 1/p))` for both populations. For the conditional population (zero-residue class removed, p-1 classes remain), comparing against 1/p over p classes embeds a structural floor of roughly 1/p and would confound the very comparison the research question asks about (unconditional vs conditional discrepancy). Constitution VII requires 'the appropriate uniform reference for each population'. The plan must state explicitly whether conditional TV uses uniform over the p-1 surviving classes (1/(p-1)) or 1/p, and apply it consistently in Phase 4, the schema descriptions, and the manuscript hand-off.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 5 / FR-010; data-model.md summary CSV schema
concerns.text: monotonicity_flag is a property of the whole ordered N-sequence, yet the summary schema places it on each per-N row with no statement of whether all rows carry the same sequence-level flag or whether the flag is only meaningful on the final row. Ambiguity here could produce inconsistent reporting of reversals; state the convention (e.g. flag repeated on every row, computed over the full supplied list).

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 4 – TV Computation / research.md 'TV calculation' row
concerns.text: Conditional TV is computed as 0.5*sum(|freq - 1/p|) over all p residue classes, with the zero class forced to freq 0. Against a p-class uniform reference this TV has a hard floor of 1/(2p) (the zero class alone contributes |0-1/p|/2), so conditional discrepancy can never approach 0 by construction — the analysis cannot distinguish genuine imbalance among nonzero residues from this definitional floor. Constitution VII requires the 'appropriate uniform reference for each population'; for the conditional population that is arguably uniform over the p-1 nonzero classes. The plan must state explicitly which reference is used and why, or the monotonicity/decrease question (the core research question) is partially answered by definition.

Monotonicity is assessed over only the 4 supplied N values with a binary OK/REVERSAL flag. This is sound as a census report, but the plan should note (per Constitution VI) that the flag is a finite-range observation with no asymptotic implication; currently only the spec's paper hand-off mentions this limitation, not the plan's interpretation guidance.
